_comment: Patches for the Design Studio page (swatchroom/terucon/Swatchroom.html, the Swatchroom 5 export): the shell template only. The studio inside is not patched: it is the swatchroom's own plain-JavaScript app, loaded from /js/swatchroom-app.js. Format: site/patches/README.md

steps.why: rewrite the design-time file names to the pages of the site
menu: My project card
steps.anchor: Sheets, stone, terracotta and finishes, priced per unit.

steps.why: footer: My project link
menu: Inspiration card
steps.anchor: Sheets, stone, terracotta and finishes, priced per unit.

steps.why: menu: Finder card
steps.anchor: Sheets, stone, terracotta and finishes, priced per unit.

steps.why: footer: Inspiration link
footer: Finder link
footer: the export says photos and key stay in the browser; the studio saves rooms on the server (its own wording: "Rooms are saved on the server, so they open on any device that can reach it")
steps.anchor: Your photos and key stay in this browser. Renders use your own Google Cloud project.
steps.with: Your rooms are saved on our server, so they open on any device.

steps.why: start the studio's cold start as soon as this page opens (the landing page already started it; this covers a visit that skipped it or came after the services went idle)

PostHog analytics: page views, clicks and forms, and (studio page) the studio's own events, which its browser code sends to window.posthog but its server never gives a key for. The script asks GET /api/analytics, so no key is in the page

sign-in: the header link says Sign in or Account, and a request answered "please sign in" (the session ended) leads to the sign-in page. The script asks GET /api/auth/me, so nothing about the visitor is in the page

a photo cropped on the Inspiration page waits in this browser (?import=<code>); this puts it into the studio's own photo input, as if the person had chosen the file, and the studio does the rest (target C3). A module served from /inspiration/assets/, so the studio page is not edited beyond this tag

the studio's "Take a photo" hands the screen to the phone's camera app, and a heavy page can be reloaded by the phone while it is away (the photo never arrives). This opens the camera inside the page instead, and gives the studio the picture as a chosen file; with no in-page camera it falls back to the camera app or the gallery (site/brand/studio-camera.js). swatchroom/ is not touched
menu overlay: the real logo (dark overlay, no pill)
footer: the full lockup above the columns
menu overlay on a phone: the five destinations first as large tap targets, then Account and Start a project (shown by the page style below; the cards for the same pages are hidden there)

insert.blurb: You are here. Upload a photo of your space and see it in Terucon materials.

steps.why: menu overlay on a phone: a small heading over the links to the home page sections
menu overlay: mark the cards column so the phone style can hide the page cards (the destinations list above replaces them)

the site chrome (site/brand/chrome.js) is the one header and, on a laptop, the sidebar: the export's own header is not drawn once the chrome is on, and the studio sits below the pill and to the right of the sidebar; the menu overlay on a phone leads with the destinations; the studio frame above the bottom bar, room under the footer
insert:
<style>
/* the site chrome is the one header (site/brand/chrome.md); the export's own header stays in the page but is not drawn while the chrome is on. The studio measures the header above it (its --swr-top) and, with none drawn, the room the chrome's pill takes */
html.tc-chrome-on [data-nav] { display: none !important; }
/* menu overlay on a phone or small tablet: destinations lead */
[data-menu-dest] { display: none; }
@media (max-width: 819px) {
  [data-menu-dest] { display: flex; }
  [data-menu] > div { justify-content: flex-start !important; gap: 26px !important; padding: 12px 20px calc(28px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)) !important; }
  [data-menu-aside] > a { display: none !important; }
  [data-menu] nav a { font-size: 22px !important; padding: 13px 0 !important; }
}
/* bottom bar: the studio frame stops above it (while the working view is not full screen) and the page gets room at its end */
@media (max-width: 899px) {
  body::after { display: none !important; }
  .tc-dock-on:not(.swr-immersive) swatchroom-app .sr-studio { height: calc(100dvh - var(--swr-top, 0px) - var(--tc-dock-h, 0px)) !important; }
  .tc-dock-on [data-studio] { padding-bottom: calc(var(--tc-dock-h, 0px) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)); }
}
</style>

steps.why: mobile dock: the bottom bar with the five destinations on a phone (site/brand/dock.md); hidden by dock.css while the studio works full screen (html.swr-immersive)

one loader on the way into the studio (site/brand/studio-entry.js holds the page loader until the studio's own first screen exists): hide the runtime's grey placeholder for the <x-import> while the studio's script loads, and the studio's own "Powered by Terucon India" splash, which would otherwise paint over the page loader (same z-index, later in the page). The splash's own timer still removes it; swatchroom/ is not touched
every "Start a project" link opens its own page, /start-project, instead of the landing page's form at the bottom (/#enquire)

the studio's own loader only imports /js/swatchroom-app.js. This one first adds the catalogue's designs to the studio's finish list (site/catalogue-ui/studio-finishes.js: a group "Terucon catalogue" for wall, door and furniture, read from MongoDB), waits at most 4 s for it, and then starts the studio whatever happened. The studio builds its index of finishes only when it first looks one up, so they have to be in its list before it starts. swatchroom/ is not touched
